people.gloss: Green moss, her Dao name, from Vương Duy's 'and shines again upon the green moss'
people.role: Keeper of the lamp oil and the guests' millet
people.appearance: Oil-dark fingertips; she sniffs every jar before she signs for it.
people.backstory: A pine-village girl who walked up in 1118, she keeps the lamp oil and feeds guests millet at dusk. She agrees with the prior Kha Thủy Cùng (kha_thuy_cung) that the reading should end, and has said so to the Reader's face. She sells a jar of the oil a month at Lam Yên Thị and tells Kha thieves took it; he pays the gap from his own allowance.

people.gloss: Empty green, his Dao name, from Vương Duy's 'the empty green wets one's clothes'
people.role: Teaches letters at the Bách Diệp school
people.appearance: Grey stubble shaved on feast days only; ears reddened by the cold.
people.backstory: Trang Thanh Tuyền's (trang_thanh_tuyen) fellow teacher at Bách Diệp, he walks the stillest children up the mountain each autumn. He walked Lao Hồng Diệp (lao_hong_diep) up from the school in 1196 and still asks after her red-leaf trade. He left Lao Hồng Diệp alone at the water's end her first night to test her sitting; she came back without two toenails and says it was her own idea.

people.role: Lime-burner's daughter turned away by Thúy Vi's outer gate
people.appearance: Lime-white knuckles; a habit of apologising to the floor.
people.backstory: Thúy Vi's outer gate turned her away for an Earth root in 1196, and Phạm Thủ Điền (pham_thu_dien) sent her on to the abbey with a note. Nông Bạch Thạch (nong_bach_thach), from her own lime village, teaches her the walk.

people.role: Ridge servant's child; carries salt and letters to the abbey kitchen
people.appearance: Bright red scarf too long for her; satchel smelling of salt.
people.backstory: A Thúy Vi ridge servant's child, she carries the Cliff Hall cook's salt and letters up to Cừ Tùng Gian (cu_tung_gian) in the abbey kitchen, and reads the letters on the way. She skims a pinch from every sack and tops it with ash; Cừ's millet has tasted wrong since the thaw, and the abbey blames him.

ties.note: she brings him his uncle's letters

people.role: Cuts and counts the mica at Vân Mẫu Khoáng
people.appearance: Mica glitter dusted in his eyebrows; a slow, flat-footed walk.
people.backstory: He digs beside Thông Vân Thạch (thong_van_thach) and counts every sheet for Lãnh Xuân Giản (lanh_xuan_gian). He has seen the new seam and been told, like Thông, to keep digging and tell no one. He counts the sheets once a week and fills in the other days' tallies from memory, so Lãnh Xuân Giản's (lanh_xuan_gian) ledger runs a pane or two off.

people.gloss: Cassia flowers, her Dao name, from Vương Duy's 'idle, the cassia flowers fall'
people.role: Young monk who carries the Reader's bell
people.appearance: Shaved head, a pale half-moon on the left palm where the bell rope sits.
people.backstory: She passed the walk in 1196 and took the name Quế Hoa. She carries the bell for Văn Nhân Hưởng (van_nhan_huong) to Không Sơn Viện each year and waits outside till dawn, and has begun to wish she could go in. She told Lao Hồng Diệp (lao_hong_diep) the night and the road of the reading, a secret she swore on the bell to keep for the Reader.

people.role: Yên Ba merchant's daughter at the school who cannot sit still
people.appearance: Good boots, mud to the knee; her fingers drum on everything within reach.
people.backstory: Her father pays the Bách Diệp school to make her sit still. Trang Thanh Tuyền (trang_thanh_tuyen) has walked her to the water's end three times; she was gone before dusk each time, and came back up next morning on her own. She watched Hỗ Kinh Điểu (ho_kinh_dieu) slip on the stream-stones and went on up the mountain without turning.
